risks.note: Conflicts, travel advisories, airspace restrictions, sanctions and aviation incidents may disrupt important travel corridors and affect demand patterns. This is not theoretical for TBO: FY 2026 saw an India-Pakistan flare-up, the broader Iran-US-Israel conflict, aviation disruptions, a major air tragedy and weather events, and March 2026 - a seasonally important period - affected both source and destination markets across approximately 40% of relevant travel corridors, producing weaker demand, cancellations and volatility in booking patterns. Airspace restrictions and instability in the Middle East are stated to have caused a 70% drop in demand in early 2026. Management's mitigation is geographic diversification across source markets, broader supply coverage, active corridor monitoring and reallocation toward alternate demand flows, and it explicitly concedes that diversification reduces exposure but does not eliminate volatility and that corridor risk remains real. Geopolitical Conflicts was newly ADDED as a BRSR material topic in FY 2025-26.
risks.risk: Geopolitical and regional disruption of travel corridors

risks.note: As a global B2B platform managing high-volume transactional, payment and customer data streams across multiple jurisdictions, the Company faces material operational and compliance exposure from systemic IT vulnerabilities; prolonged network outages, infrastructure failures or sophisticated cyber incidents can immediately disrupt downstream booking fulfilment, cause revenue leakage and severely compromise partner trust. Privacy and Data Security is the FIRST-listed BRSR material issue, rated both risk and opportunity, with the stated negative implication being exposure to legal penalties and significant breach-recovery costs. Mitigation is stated as enterprise-grade threat detection, data encryption, regular assessments, access controls, platform resilience, monitoring and audit, and strict compliance with applicable data-privacy regulations. The Corporate Governance Report separately makes cybersecurity and data protection a standing board-level oversight area.

AI-enabled interfaces and agentic commerce models may increasingly influence how travel is discovered, planned, booked and fulfilled, creating intermediary bypass risk in simpler use cases. This is the risk most specific to the business model and management engages it directly rather than deflecting: its stated counter-thesis is that complex, premium and multi-component travel will continue to require expertise, robust fulfilment infrastructure, curated supply, servicing capability, payment infrastructure and operational reliability, and that AI bots will become demand channels FEEDING travel distribution platforms rather than replacing them. Mitigation is continued investment in AI-enabled workflows, infrastructure relevance, fulfilment capability and advisor-led complex travel. Note the two-sided nature: management also frames AI as a moat risk in the other direction, observing that frontier models can recreate an entire platform front-end at a fraction of cost and time, which is why it argues differentiation must sit in infrastructure, integrations, relationships and data systems rather than interface.
risks.risk: AI-driven disintermediation of the distribution channel

risks.note: The business model depends on relationships with airlines, hotel chains, aggregators and ancillary providers, and changes in supplier economics, commission structures, pricing models or direct distribution strategies may affect profitability and competitiveness. The structural exposure is that suppliers can choose to go direct and bypass the distribution layer. Mitigation is expansion of direct contracting (direct supply share rose to 35% in FY 2026 from 33.9% in FY 2025), diversified supplier relationships and long-term partnership management.

The market remains highly competitive with global online travel companies, regional platforms, supplier-direct channels and specialist vertical players participating; competitive intensity may increase pressure on pricing, commissions, customer acquisition costs and margins. Mitigation is stated as continued investment in technology, servicing capability, supply breadth, premium travel positioning and differentiated partner workflows.
risks.risk: Competitive intensity in global travel distribution

risks.note: Inflation, interest rates, currency movements and slower discretionary spending may affect booking volumes, travel frequency, destination choices and traveller spend; currency weakness in outbound source markets may specifically affect affordability and mix. Travel is discretionary, so this risk is amplified relative to staples-like businesses. Mitigation is diversified market exposure, product mix toward higher-value categories, active commercial management and customer-cohort diversification.

Not presented in the AR's risk table but flagged repeatedly by management as a live watch-item: hiring sales teams and adding feet-on-street carries upfront cost, newly onboarded agents take time to activate, mature and scale, and the full operating leverage from the FY 2026 investment cycle will emerge only over time as cohorts become more productive and the cost base stabilises. Management states these investments elevated SG&A growth in the first half of FY 2026 before moderating from Q3 FY 2026, and concedes that 'sales investments can create future growth, but they also carry upfront costs before operating leverage is fully visible' and that 'AI improves productivity, but it does not transform operating models overnight'.
risks.risk: Execution and cost-timing risk in the commercial investment cycle

risks.note: The North America strategy rests on a single acquisition. Management describes the integration - spanning platform, supply, commercial and talent - as an execution priority with expected completion by Q3 of the current fiscal (stated as FY 2027 in the Letter to Shareholders) and explicitly characterises it as 'a multi-year value creation journey' that is 'not complete'. The stated intent is not simply to consolidate Classic Vacations but to combine its advisor relationships, luxury supply and servicing expertise with TBO's technology, global supply network, commercial reach and operating discipline - a two-way integration that is correspondingly harder to execute.
risks.risk: Integration risk on the Classic Vacations acquisition and dependence on M&A for the North America build

ins.thesis: TBO is a global B2B travel-distribution platform monetizing GTV via take-rate, with structural growth from (a) market-development investment (sales/KAM expansion → onboarding new travel agents and driving them through T1/T5/T10 transaction journey), (b) shift toward higher-take-rate markets (North America, Europe) and higher-margin hotels mix vs air, and (c) the luxury/curated adjacency (Classic Vacations + Voya AI tool). Q4FY26 demonstrated resilience: despite the war (started end-Feb) severely hitting its largest source market (Middle East) and Israel (a Top-7 source country), the company still grew YoY on both top and bottom line. Jan/Feb showed strong operating leverage and margin expansion, March was "a complete washout." Mgmt expects Q1FY27 better than both Q4 and the year-ago quarter, with green shoots of operating leverage as SG&A growth tapers below GTV growth.
